Cuu Non Hy Lap: Great Inexpensive Greek Food and a Unique Vietnamese Story
Dec 2018
Cuu Non Hy Lap, with its tasty and authentic Greek delicacies and casual outdoor dining, is a unique and memorable Saigon experience, matched only by the unique and memorable character of its owner/chef. District 3’s roadside Greek restaurant across from the river has a story with a unique and amazing twist: restaurant owner and chef Duc is Vietnamese . . . and then became Greek. How? you might ask.

Duc's story is a tale of courage, resilience and triumph. He was a teenage refugee who crossed stormy seas to reach Malaysia. Soon he was on a plane with other Vietnamese refugees and landed in a place he never imagined he’d visit: Athens, Greece.

His education - learning a new language and learning about life and survival in a foreign land - came through work. He started out in restaurant kitchens working long hours as a dish hand and cleaner. He made Greek friends quickly through his work ethic and quick wit, learned the language fluently, and progressed in the restaurant industry to eventually become a chef. He worked hard and did well, but when the global financial crisis hit in 2008 he realised that he had one more calling: to return to his original home, Vietnam.

Duc started over in the country of his birth, and before long was back in business, opening his own restaurant, Cuu Non Hy Lap (Greek Lamb). It is a restaurant that offers a variety of cuisines, but what makes it special are the Greek dishes cooked 7 days a week by Duc himself. Try any of his signature dishes - moussaka, meat barbecued Greek-style on the grill, tasty and authentic dips, delicious cheese pies (tiropitakia) made with filo pastry - and you will know that these are meals cooked with love and skill. 

Duc is a proud Vietnamese man. And he is also a proud Greek citizen. He is an extraordinary man who is only too happy to share his food and his story (in English, Vietnamese or Greek!) with his loyal and satisfied customers. Tell him Milton says hello when you go there.

Excellent Greek Food
Sep 2018 • Friends
This restaurant was favourably reviewed in a Saigon magazine, so we went there at sunset. 
What a surprise! The tables and chairs were well placed for views of the river and bridge. The service was excellent.
The beer was chilled.
The Greek food was delicious. Greek salad, moussaka, lamb kebab, garlic bread. A huge meal for 2 people, including 6 beers, for 444,000 VND (= $18).
Will definitely visit this place again and again.
